(Remove Chat Moderator) Proposed by Printer89[]

On the wiki, the chat is barely used by users. It has a good purpose; however, the most popular way for users to interact is using the forums and/or blogs. I propose removing the ability for users to request for Chat Moderator rights and instead allow users to request for Discussion Moderator rights instead.

Support

  1. Yeah I'd have to agree. While chat is used from time to time it is nowhere near as active as forums, blogs or even the discord. --Toa Kopaka Nuva (talk) 03:46, June 20, 2020 (UTC)

Oppose

  1. While it is not very active now, it could become more active in the future. And, yes, chat mod rights are already included in discussion mod rights, but there could be people that are specifically interested in moderating the chat and not the forums/blogs.Ninja72 (talk) 04:30, June 20, 2020 (UTC)
  2. Agreed. Just because it is inactive doesn't mean it won't be active. Lego Ninjago Fan 2006 (talk) 12:06, June 20, 2020 (UTC)

Neutral

Comments

To comment on this, fandom plans on disabling the chat feature in their UCP update so I don't see it becoming more active in the future. --Toa Kopaka Nuva (talk) 04:35, June 20, 2020 (UTC)

This request was dropped by the owner.

(Add Discussions, then eventually remove forums) by Unfortunate 666[]

Out of all the wikis I've been to, less than 5 have forums, and over 5 have discussions. Ninjago Wiki will eventually have discussions, and they will replace forums entirely. I'm proposing to add discussions, then remove forums within 2-12 months, since I learned that forums and discussions can be at the same time.

Support

  1. Yeah, I guess we could. Discussions are gonna come, willingly or unwillingly. Lego Ninjago Fan 2006 (talk) 16:04, June 20, 2020 (UTC)

Oppose

  1. Forums are way more organized than discussions. And on discussions, there is no way of editing your comments. There is also the fact that discussions are separated from the main site and due to this, the community on discussion could become a completely different community from the one on the main site. I think we should just enjoy the last months in which we are not forced to use that horrible feature.Ninja72 (talk) 16:24, June 20, 2020 (UTC)
  2. Same reason I listed in the comments. --Toa Kopaka Nuva (talk) 22:18, August 1, 2020 (UTC)
  3. It will come, I agree, but for now I think we should keep it how it is. As Ninja72 said, it is more organized. --NinjaBrix (talk) 22:24, August 1, 2020 (UTC)
  4. I do not want the forums to be removed. I will not vote for anything else. LuigiMaster41 (talk) 22:37, August 1, 2020 (UTC)
  5. It can wait. Quinton1721, He Who Will Fight All of Asia 17:02, August 2, 2020 (UTC)

Neutral

  1. The Eternal Equalizer 16:32, June 20, 2020 (UTC)
  2. I think that it will come whether we like it or not but I'm not necessarily a fan of it as I agree with Ninja72 and think forums are more organized. --NinjaBrix (talk) 16:47, June 20, 2020 (UTC)

Comments

It's worth noting that this is Fandom's exact plan. While we can request Discussions for the wiki, Fandom will be removing Forums from all wikis soon and replacing them with Discussions. Personally I'd only like to have one open at the same time so that all focus is in the same place.

So I say we wait until Fandom does this in a few months. --Toa Kopaka Nuva (talk) 16:05, June 20, 2020 (UTC)

Doesn't Brickipedia have forums and discussions. I checked it before. Lego Ninjago Fan 2006 (talk) 16:12, June 20, 2020 (UTC)

Yes, but it was set up that way by Fandom. I had no say and wish that we didn't have both. --Toa Kopaka Nuva (talk) 16:45, June 20, 2020 (UTC)

I'd like to correct a statement by Ninja72 that you can edit your comments in Discussions, up until 24 hours, unless you are a Discussions Moderator/Admin. Quinton1721, He Who Will Fight All of Asia 17:02, August 2, 2020 (UTC)

The result of the vote was: Oppose

(Make an Age subpage) by Wikifan988[]

The information about the ninjas' ages (except Zane for the most part) in their "Age" sections are all connected to each other and rely on statements about other characters' ages to some degree, especially in Nya and Lloyd's cases. Or at least most of the information overlaps and has to be restated on each page, such as how they won't age past being teenagers.

I think it would be more efficient if there was one page for ages, I'm thinking it could be Ninja (Team)/Ages, which lists all the information in one place, and each character's "Age" section links to this the same way that transcripts/relationships/histories/galleries do. (I know in those cases it's a singular page/subpage connection but it would generally work the same way.) Maybe the page could have three sections, one for the five human Ninja (or one for the original three and two shorter sections for Nya and Lloyd), one for Zane, and one for Wu and Garmadon.

If this exact system doesn't sound like it would work, I'm open to suggestions for other ways it could be accomplished, but overall I think it may be beneficial to consolidate all the information. People not familiar with the crew statements are likely to wonder about the characters' ages and I think it would be better to have a more visible and specific page for it, which newcomers could go to to learn all the age information at once and be able to easily refer back to it when needed.

At the very least, this would prevent having to edit every page's age section if you wanted to change the way something on them was phrased, for example.

Support

Oppose

  1. Printer89 (talk) 12:23, July 14, 2020 (UTC)
  2. Ninja72 (talk) 12:40, July 14, 2020 (UTC)

Neutral

Comments

I'm all for it but there should be big note that the specific age for the characters in the Show was never mentioned and page consist only the known facts and assumptions. MysticMiracle000 (talk) 06:28, July 14, 2020 (UTC)

I agree, that would definitely have to be on there. Wikifan988 (talk) 06:56, July 14, 2020 (UTC)

I think this suggestion has some good points, but sub-pages are typically made because the main page is too big and the information you want on the sub-page has too much information. There isn't that much content on each of the age section, and you can edit each of the age pages pretty easily due to the lack of content. Printer89 (talk) 12:23, July 14, 2020 (UTC)

This request was dropped by the owner.

(Disallow links in quotes) by Wikifan988[]

I hope it's okay that I'm adding multiple suggestions at the same time. I think it would be good to instate a rule where no links can be used in page quotes. This is because it's a distraction from the quote itself to see the links and to wonder what they're linking to (especially with words like "I" and "we"). The links also become hard to see on pages that use a darker blue or green color for the quote box. Lastly, a quote is meant to provide a quick general context of the page or give a humorous insight on the topic, but if there are links in the quote it takes away from the straightforward nature of this.

Support

Oppose

Neutral

  1. Printer89 (talk) 12:23, July 14, 2020 (UTC)

Comments

It may provide issues for some, but I feel like links are important in quotes because readers would know the context of what's going on. Printer89 (talk) 12:23, July 14, 2020 (UTC)

This request was dropped by the owner.

(Add "smear frames" slideshow gallery to Vlad Tutu and Let's Dance! pages) by Wikifan988[]

I added to the trivia on Vlad Tutu's page noting how his character often used the animation technique known as "smear frames," and I think it would be cool to have a slideshow gallery next to this note or after the normal gallery, that would include all the frames where the character is stretched out. This would allow readers who are interested in this to look at them, without taking up much space if they aren't interested. Printer89 suggested I bring this here. (Site Rename) by Toa Kopaka Nuva[]

As I said in my July Update, "My goal is to in time, build up the site so that it can become a recognized LEGO Online Community. This will not only help us build connections with other LEGO Fans, but also LEGO themselves. However, due to restrictions on how LEGO’s trademarks (such as Ninjago) can be used, we will need to change the wiki name and URL. I am willing to discuss this with everyone, but I do feel it is the best path to take. This would be a major change for the wiki and whatever direction we take should have a large amount of support."

Its time for us to discuss the potential name change. The biggest reason for this change is so that we can potentially get connected with LEGO via the LEGO Ambassador Network. This would greatly help us to get more connected to the LEGO community and support us when Ninjago eventually ends. From LEGO's Website The LEGO Ambassador Network is "the platform and network foundation on which we base all our communication and support for the recognized entities of the AFOL community. The LAN is where ambassadors from the various recognized communities share experiences, get help and interact with other recognized communities and the LEGO Group AFOL Engagement Department". Many LEGO fan-websites (Brickset, TheBrickfan) and Youtubers (Just2Good) are members of this program, however we are currently ineligible solely due to our site name containing "Ninjago".

A rename is not a short or easy process and I want it to potentially go the best it can. The main issue that comes with renaming is that our SEO (Google Placement) will reset temporarily. There isn’t much that that can be done to prevent this from happening, however, cases like Brickipedia show that it is recoverable. Again I’ll be in touch with Fandom to ensure this is done properly and if it is the right way to go. If we do go through with the name change, the process would take place in September/ October. This is typically a slow time for us and I don’t feel we would be hurt by a lower SEO during this time.

This vote is not guaranteeing that the rename will take place (as Fandom could tell us no) but it will allow me to start communicating with Fandom on the process.

Also, this vote is not determining a name (Although most people seemed to like Ninjapedia) --Toa Kopaka Nuva (talk) 23:29, July 19, 2020 (UTC)

(Merge all Cards pages) by Wikifan988[]

  • Most of the information is duplicated on every page, or is evident from the card image: Stats is on the card, How to Use and Requirements are the same for every card with only some minor differences on some of the pages that are from different users editing them different ways, and the information in the infobox can either be gleaned from the card's appearance or would be evident from the card's placement in the list if the pages were to be merged into one list like Types of Ninja.
  • I think it is fair to say each individual card is less notable than each ninja suit, so if those are merged, the cards should be too, in my opinion.
  • It would be easier to navigate for readers who wanted to see all the cards (for the illustrations, for example), rather than having to click through every page to see the images (or in the cases of the Character Cards, the images in regular size).
  • It would be much easier in the future for possible format changes because now every card page would not have to be edited individually. If it would be too much to have them all on one page, then it can be split into two, one for 2011 and 2012. (Or another division for both, for characters.)

So if they were all merged on the page, the information about how to use the cards would be at the top of the page (this is already the case on the Cards page), and then every card would be listed as a section, with its image, "Where to Find," and Notes/Trivia as the information for each card. I'm imagining the format as something like Types of Ninja but it could also be done as a grid sort of format like a larger version of what's on List of Ninjago Cast and Characters.

Support

Oppose

  1. I strongly oppose this, it can increase loading times when editing the page. That's a big hard no from me. LuigiMaster41 (talk) 22:31, August 10, 2020 (UTC)
  2. Vehemently strong oppose. Unfortunate 666 11:20, August 12, 2020 (UTC)

Neutral

Comments

If they were to be separated into two of four pages, I think there would not be much more on each page than there is on Types of Ninja. Also, I know editing is an important factor, but it is also important to think about it from a reader/casual visitor's perspective. Also, I don't think this is a problem if one is using source editor. Wikifan988 (talk) 19:24, August 11, 2020 (UTC)

I appreciate you making a valid point Wikifan, however, I stand by my decision, oppose. LuigiMaster41 (talk) 19:50, August 11, 2020 (UTC)

(Rename P.I.X.A.L. to Pixal) by Wikifan988[]

  • She is called Pixal in the sets and the sets take precedence over the show's credits in other cases such as Skales, especially since the show credits can often have errors (sometimes have said "Ronan" or "Skyler"/"Skylar"). (It's worth noting that she is even called "Pixal" in some of the credits too, or at least Curseworld Part I is one example I know of.)
  • Tommy Andreasen always calls her Pixal or PIXAL but never P.I.X.A.L.[3][4] While you could say this is because it's easier to type (which is also likely true), it's still a good reason/evidence to support that her official name is not the one the current page is called. (Edit: this is also the case with the Hageman Brothers[5][6])
  • Her March of the Oni poster just says PIXAL.
  • It is unnecessary for editors to have to type P.I.X.A.L. every time, and other pages like Jay and Lloyd are named the way they are because it would be a hassle to link their full name every time they are mentioned, even if their extended names are technically their more official names. (Though I understand that in these contexts most pages would already be referring to them as just Jay or Lloyd, rather than how the way P.I.X.A.L.'s name is visibly written would have to be changed as well in this Pixal case.)
  • Yes it is an acronym, but you could say that as Pixal has moved beyond her initial assistant android status, her name has also evolved beyond its initial meaning and is now thought of as more of a regular name rather than a robot name, both in the show (they also call her "Pix") and by fans/creators of the show.

While some may be opposed to this because it would be a lot of changes to make since she is a major character who is mentioned on hundreds of pages, that is true, but the fact that something is already done a certain way should never be the main reason to not change it. Also it would not be too hard to implement this change if a bot was used, from my understanding. Also, this change would make it easier to mention in every future article or future episode page.

Oppose

(Merge all Ninjago Wildlife pages) by Wikifan988[]

Each page consists of an official description and image from LEGO.com, and someone's summary of the description. I think it would be more efficient/methodical to have all of these official descriptions on one page with the images next to the corresponding descriptions, because the creatures and plants here are not things that have ever appeared in the show and it's very unlikely that they will appear at this point, and it's not known if they are canon either. (If one of them did appear in the show then that one would be given its own page, similar to how the more notable Skulkin Vehicles have their own pages while the others don't.) The resulting page would be similar to the LEGO.com Descriptions sections on the Ninja pages, as well as the way Types of Ninja is organized. The original pages could be kept as redirects so their page histories will not be lost.

Unlike other species who are in the show, every "Ninjago Wildlife" entry only exists in having come from the LEGO.com website at one point along with all the others (same description style, art style, etc). It is essentially a locked set like the Ninja vs. Snakes Activity Books. I think this type of content better lends itself to one longer page rather than split into many shorter pages, as it is easier for readers to navigate when just learning about it and is also easier for editors to change any links or formatting on just one page instead of many.

A side effect of this would be that Template:Animals and Template:Food are largely cut down on pages they link to. However, I think in the Animals template's case, this could be helpful anyway because there's already mostly a duplicate of information with the Animals template and the Creatures section of Template:People. Either the Animals not already on People could be migrated there and the Animals template could be deleted, or the Creatures section of People could be moved to Animals since People is already a large enough anyway in my opinion. (I prefer the second option.) But this is only a side effect/secondary concern.

Thanks for reading, sorry for the long proposal, I just wanted to explain all my reasoning behind it.

Support

  1. It is unnecessary to have such short pages and no one will probably search for them anyway, because they are not in the show.Ninja72 (talk) 12:41, August 18, 2020 (UTC)

Oppose

  1. LuigiMaster41, Master of Lightning 12:32, August 17, 2020 (UTC)
  2. The Eternal Equalizer 19:54, August 17, 2020 (UTC)

Neutral

Comments

(Merge the four Pilot Episode pages into just two) by Wikifan988[]

Merge "Way of the Ninja" and "The Golden Weapon" into just Way of the Ninja, and "King of Shadows" and "Weapons of Destiny" into just King of Shadows. The creators consider them as two episodes[7][8] (it's true they also refer to them as just "the pilot" but this tweet is referring to them in a more technical/specific context where Tommy Andreasen is explaining the episode numbering) so that means they were intended to be that way and any division of them is less official. And all the other normal episodes for the next ten seasons were 22 minutes. I don't know what the original reason was on the wiki for having them as four separate episodes, but if was just what LEGO.com and/or some airings of it said, I don't think that is enough to keep them separated. Naturally we would note this division situation on the pages in the Trivia section, but I think in general it makes more sense to count them as 22-minute episodes.

(Not captalise parentheses in article titles) by LuigiMaster41[]

Hello, Ninjago Wiki users! LuigiMaster41 here, and I have an idea that is not by be, but rather from User:Wikifan988. This idea is mainly to not capitalise parentheses in article titles. Here is the idea:

From Wikifan988: This would be a very big change, but have the parentheses notes in titles not be capitalized unless it's something that is naturally capitalized like in "The Resistance (Never-Realm)." So for example, The Green Ninja (Book) would be The Green Ninja (book). This would be more consistent with Wikipedia and other wikis, and I think it would be more "official" formatting overall since these labels are not part of the title which is the only reason why something should be capitalized. It also is unnecessary to refer to the these things with capitalization, because it weakens the meaning of capitalization, which is only for proper names/titles and beginnings of sentences really. Along with this, statuses of characters/installments/etc. would also not be capitalized, so things would always be (non-canon) rather than (Non-canon), same with (Formerly), etc. (Both versions are used currently, this would just homogenize it). Also for the titles, including the cases listed below, it would be easier to link to them in other articles (writing [[skeleton figurehead]] or [[Skeleton figurehead]] instead of [[Skeleton Figurehead|Skeleton figurehead]]), since in both of these cases the capitalization is not how you would refer to them on other pages since they are not proper names. Also, having only proper names and titles be capitalized gives them more attention as the subjects of the sentence/line/etc. It also is technically speculation to name things as if the article titles are their official names, if the names themselves are not official, and having them be capitalized indicates that they are official names. Some other notable wikis do this (including Wikipedia) and I think it is the better option. While it would be a lot to change, that should not be the main reason for not doing something. We also already have (disambiguation) uncapitalized and that too is just a page identifier. Also, like Wikipedia says, "words [should not be] capitalized unless they would be so in running text."

So that is Wikifan988's idea, now, please feel free to voice your opinions!

Support

  1. Wikifan988 (talk) 20:51, August 22, 2020 (UTC)

Oppose

  2. Too much renaming to do for such a minor change. As for the titles, you can just add a NoName template to the main article to show it's not an official name. Printer89 (talk) 14:17, August 23, 2020 (UTC)

I think it would help because it would make the wiki consistent, since (formerly) and those types of notes within articles aren't meant to be capitalized either nowadays (and from what I understand at least, when they are it is mostly remnants from when it used to always be done this way), and it is always good to be consistent when possible. Wikifan988 (talk) 21:13, August 22, 2020 (UTC)

(Allow episode citations in some cases) by Wikifan988[]

There are certain cases, often history sections for characters referring to times from before the series starts (such as Garmadon, Wu, and First Spinjitzu Master's pages) or races/realms with a lot of history like Ninjago or the Oni, that do not really work to have "Episode Name (Flashback)" as the headings for the information. However, this leads to the problem where the information is not cited. So my proposal is to allow episode citations (like this[1]) on information in these contexts. Though there doesn't need to be a source for things that are stated/shown in many episodes, like Kai and Nya's parents having disappeared when they were young, for example. This is only for information that is primarily gained from one or two episodes. Another example of this type of information would be character names, where a character's full name is only said in one episode, that episode should be cited next to their name in the same way tweets or official books are cited for other page's names. (Though again if it's a one-installment character, it's not necessary.)

  1. ↑ Episode Name

This allows readers to know exactly where the information is coming, from which makes the wiki feel more reliable, and it helps to prevent speculation or conjecture if everything in these non-episode-listed contexts requires a source. Also, new readers or newcomers to Ninjago could be likely to want to see the episodes where something that looks interesting to them is from, and this makes it very easy to find this out without having to click onto other pages and cross-reference the Appearances section with what says (flashback) next to it or anything more complicated like that. The one caveat could be that some people could find it distracting, but I don't think that is too much of an issue since tweets and official books are already cited this way on the wiki, and many popular wikis do this where they cite installments from the main work (such as Arrowverse Wiki or Harry Potter Wiki).

Support

  1. I'd love for us to start doing this. Sometimes it is hard to know where information is coming from and this would be very helpful. Wikis such as Wookiepedia do this and it works well for them. --Toa Kopaka Nuva (talk) 13:47, August 22, 2020 (UTC)
  2. I'll support this, but I think we should still keep "Episode Name (Flashback)". If that's not the case, I'm placing my vote back in oppose. LuigiMaster41 (talk) 13:52, August 22, 2020 (UTC)
  3. I have thought about it for some time and I now see how this would make it easier for people who do not remember exactly which episode the flashback was in, as they would not have to scroll down and see the appearances section to see exactly which episode it was.Ninja72 (talk) 19:17, August 25, 2020 (UTC)

Oppose

  1. Why exactly must we make this change? LuigiMaster41 (talk) 13:41, August 22, 2020 (UTC)

Neutral

Comments

It wouldn't be replacing the Episode Name (Flashback) system, it would just be citing episodes in situations where it doesn't make sense to use that format. Wikifan988 (talk) 16:26, August 22, 2020 (UTC)

@Wikifan So we are keeping Episode Name (Flashback) format? If so, I'm in! If not... LuigiMaster41 (talk) 18:48, August 22, 2020 (UTC)

That's right. So for example, citations will be added to Garmadon's pre-series biography since those are not already using the (Flashback) format and changing them would be getting rid of the more descriptive headings they already have. Citations like this would often be used in Early life sections. Also I had previously added the Flashback format to pages such as Dr. Julien and the three original ninja, but if citations are allowed then I would change it back because the (Flashback) format wasn't there before I edited them, and I was only editing them this way since at that point episode citations would have not been allowed. Wikifan988 (talk) 19:01, August 22, 2020 (UTC)

Ah, I see. This seems like good organisation you have and I want to give it my full support! LuigiMaster41 (talk) 19:09, August 22, 2020 (UTC)

The result of the vote was: Support

(Add "Installment" parameter to set infoboxes or mention the installment in intro descriptions) by Wikifan988[]

Most sets coincide with an installment (either a season, Day of the Departed, or the movie) and currently there is no easy way to find out what installment the set is meant to coincide with or to navigate to that installment's page. While it's true that people who know the series well will already know, the wiki is not just for people who know the series well, and in my mind, the installment a set was released to coincide with is around the same level of significance as the set's release date. Though the release date is already there, casual readers will not necessarily associate a date with an installment like fans of the series will. So I am proposing to either add a parameter to the set infoboxes to list the installment, or to change the introduction format to something like "Blaster Bike is a LEGO Ninjago: Masters of Spinjitzu Season 5 set released in 2015." Sets with no specific installment could say N/A or not include this parameter, while Legacy set pages would stay the way they are for now.

I was originally on the opinion that we should keep it as Paleman, because he is only called Mr. Pale once in the show and it could have been an error like how in Season 4 they were calling Shade Shadow instead of Shade and as far as I knew the only other place he is called Mr. Pale in were the credits in S4 and episode credits are full of errors. (Add an "Influence" section to applicable pages) by Wikifan988[]

For example, on Cliff Gordon's page, there would be another section called Influence which explains the events of Misfortune Rising, rather than then Misfortune Rising events being part of his History section. The reason for separating these is because the Misfortune Rising events did not directly happen to Cliff: they were a result of his existence and his actions, but not part of the life of Cliff himself. The benefit for something like this, especially on characters with longer histories, is that it separates the events that happened to the character vs the events that relate to the character but are not directly part of the character's life. Note that we would still include information in the History section if it is about the character's life even if the character does not appear in the episode. For example, the Elemental Master of Ice information from Snake Jaguar would stay in his History section.

Some other examples:

  • Garmadon: his roles, for example, in Day of the Departed, Pause and Effect, and The Explorers Club would be covered in the Influence section rather than the History section. This is because Garmadon himself was not involved in any of these events, but they are still notable events relating to him and the impact he has left on others.
  • Pythor: the times he is mentioned in The Quiet One and Questing for Quests would now be in his Influence section. The events of Blue Lightning could even be listed because are a product of someone else's (Jay's) perception of Pythor.
  • Aspheera: all her appearances and mentions after Vengeance is Mine! would go in her Influence section.

I think this would be good because it would allow the History sections to be more focused on the chronological in-universe timeline of the character, while the Influence section would allow the other information to stay on the page in a cohesive way that could serve as its own independent section as well. This also makes articles more concise because instead of having a few one-sentence paragraphs, one or two multi-sentence paragraphs can get the information across by combining them into one narration of the effects the character has had on others.

Some other notes:

  • This idea was inspired by "Legacy" sections I have seen on a few other wikis; I changed the idea to "Influence" so it could include living characters as well. See some examples of Legacy sections (which is the same type of information that would be in Influence sections) here and here.
  • At least one page already has a "Legacy" section, that being the First Spinjitzu Master.
  • An Influence section would not be necessary for a character's page if there is not any information that would go there, the same way Trivia sections are not always on pages.
  • This would also apply to non-characters when applicable. For example, the time Jay's game show is mentioned in Sons of Garmadon would be in the game show's influence section, since the show itself is not seen in the episode but it still gives more information on Jay's embarassment about the show.
  • The section would only list things that are directly related to the person, not simply anything the character has caused to happen in some way. Using Jay's mother as an example: "Jay's abandonment ultimately helped him to reason with Unagami" etc would be appropriate, but "Jay's Mother helped Jay because he used his inherited Lightning power to unlock his True Potential and save himself and Nya when they were at Mega Monster Amusement Park" etc. would not be necessary.

Sorry this proposal is so long. I wanted to describe everything as clearly as I could so it would be easy to understand what I am proposing.

(Have page names be in sentence case by default and stop trusting subtitles) by Wikifan988[]

Sentence case refers to the way something is written in a sentence. For example, in a sentence, you would write "Wu's rickshaw" rather than "Wu's Rickshaw", unless an official source wrote it as the latter. What I am proposing here is that we have pages be written this way by default, unless they are proper names. So "Wu's Rickshaw" would become "Wu's rickshaw", "Koko's Apartment" would become "Koko's apartment", and so on. This would apply to characters too, so "Fugi-Dove's Brother" would become "Fugi-Dove's brother", etc.

This is because, as SoyP777 stated in an earlier vote regarding some page names, "They should not be capitalized if it is not an actual name. We merely know that this is what the show called them, and should remain that way." All of these names are descriptive terms so they should be written in that way rather than treated as an official title. If the name is given from the credits of an episode, then it should remain capitalized because the credits are treating them as proper names. But when it is a fan-made descriptive name, or simply something said in the show that was neither clearly a proper name or a descriptive term and has no official sources indicating the name either way, it should be treated as a descriptive term because it is technically speculation to refer to it as a proper name otherwise.

A reason against renaming pages this way in the past has been that titles should always be capitalized. However, this is not always the case anymore on the wiki, because it is more accurate to have titles in lowercase/sentence case when official sources write them this way, such as purple bog frogs and several other pages. (Pages have also been created since then and given sentence case titles, due to the precedent set by the fact that not all other titles are capitalized anymore.) Additionally, it is worth noting that titles are not always capitalized in real life situations/publications. For example, newspaper headlines may not have all words capitalized, only the first word and proper names. And seeing as this wiki is an online encyclopedia, and not all encyclopedias have headings in title case, it would not be unreasonable to name pages this way on the wiki.

The other reason not to rename pages this way could be because it would require a lot of renaming and changing links in articles. However, I do not think this is a reason not to do it, because there have been many articles renamed in the past few months and it has not taken too much time overall. While it may take up some time to make this change, in the end it will result in more consistent titling of articles and more technically correct writing in articles and less need to pipe pages instead of linking to them directly. What I mean by this is that currently, there is a choice to either write "The ninja piloted [[Wu's Rickshaw]]" (which is incorrect because rickshaw would not be capitalized in a regular sentence) "The ninja piloted [[Wu's Rickshaw|Wu's rickshaw]]" (which is more work for editors and is unecessary if we could simply name the page to be in sentence case).

Along with this, I think we should stop treating episode subtitles as official sources. I realize I was the one to bring this idea about, so it is sort of my fault that this has to be proposed to reverse, but I've realized the subtitles are not reliable, as they are not made by LEGO, Cartoon Network, or the Ninjago official crew. They name things inconsistently (they say "loot box" in one scene and "Loot-Box" in another, or something similar, and "Swamp-Teeth" vs "Swamp-teeth", etc), and they contradict the more official/canon sources, such as spelling "Skales" as "Scales". They copy the spellings from the credits, which have had many errors in the past and are not considered canon in comparison to the names given in the books or sets.

But what do we do when there is no source for a name then? Well like I said, we name all "unconfirmed capitalization" pages in sentence case instead of title case. While there are probably some cases where it is very obviously meant to be a proper name, those could be handled on a case-by-case basis, and I'm sure there are more specifics that would apply to certain situations, but overall I think using sentence case for all articles unless proven otherwise is the best choice going forward.

Sorry this proposal is so long, again I wanted to make sure I made it as clear as possible what I am proposing.

(Have page names be in sentence case by default and stop trusting subtitles) by Wikifan988[]

Sentence case refers to the way something is written in a sentence. For example, in a sentence, you would write "Wu's rickshaw" rather than "Wu's Rickshaw", unless an official source wrote it as the latter. What I am proposing here is that we have pages be written this way by default, unless they are proper names. So "Wu's Rickshaw" would become "Wu's rickshaw", "Koko's Apartment" would become "Koko's apartment", and so on. This would apply to characters too, so "Fugi-Dove's Brother" would become "Fugi-Dove's brother", etc.

This is because, as SoyP777 stated in an earlier vote regarding some page names, "They should not be capitalized if it is not an actual name. We merely know that this is what the show called them, and should remain that way." All of these names are descriptive terms so they should be written in that way rather than treated as an official title. If the name is given from the credits of an episode, then it should remain capitalized because the credits are treating them as proper names. But when it is a fan-made descriptive name, or simply something said in the show that was neither clearly a proper name or a descriptive term and has no official sources indicating the name either way, it should be treated as a descriptive term because it is technically speculation to refer to it as a proper name otherwise.

A reason against renaming pages this way in the past has been that titles should always be capitalized. However, this is not always the case anymore on the wiki, because it is more accurate to have titles in lowercase/sentence case when official sources write them this way, such as purple bog frogs and several other pages. (Pages have also been created since then and given sentence case titles, due to the precedent set by the fact that not all other titles are capitalized anymore.) Additionally, it is worth noting that titles are not always capitalized in real life situations/publications. For example, newspaper headlines may not have all words capitalized, only the first word and proper names. And seeing as this wiki is an online encyclopedia, and not all encyclopedias have headings in title case, it would not be unreasonable to name pages this way on the wiki.

The other reason not to rename pages this way could be because it would require a lot of renaming and changing links in articles. However, I do not think this is a reason not to do it, because there have been many articles renamed in the past few months and it has not taken too much time overall. While it may take up some time to make this change, in the end it will result in more consistent titling of articles and more technically correct writing in articles and less need to pipe pages instead of linking to them directly. What I mean by this is that currently, there is a choice to either write "The ninja piloted [[Wu's Rickshaw]]" (which is incorrect because rickshaw would not be capitalized in a regular sentence) "The ninja piloted [[Wu's Rickshaw|Wu's rickshaw]]" (which is more work for editors and is unecessary if we could simply name the page to be in sentence case).

Along with this, I think we should stop treating episode subtitles as official sources. I realize I was the one to bring this idea about, so it is sort of my fault that this has to be proposed to reverse, but I've realized the subtitles are not reliable, as they are not made by LEGO, Cartoon Network, or the Ninjago official crew. They name things inconsistently (they say "loot box" in one scene and "Loot-Box" in another, or something similar, and "Swamp-Teeth" vs "Swamp-teeth", etc), and they contradict the more official/canon sources, such as spelling "Skales" as "Scales". They copy the spellings from the credits, which have had many errors in the past and are not considered canon in comparison to the names given in the books or sets.

But what do we do when there is no source for a name then? Well like I said, we name all "unconfirmed capitalization" pages in sentence case instead of title case. While there are probably some cases where it is very obviously meant to be a proper name, those could be handled on a case-by-case basis, and I'm sure there are more specifics that would apply to certain situations, but overall I think using sentence case for all articles unless proven otherwise is the best choice going forward.

Sorry this proposal is so long, again I wanted to make sure I made it as clear as possible what I am proposing.

To Pilot episodes, Mini-movies, and Season 4: Tournament of Elements. This is because they are referred to this way in the Visual Dictionary New Edition, as seen here. (For the first two, the "PILOT EPISODES" heading is all caps but you can see in the text below that the names are all lowercase) I realize these sorts of books have not always been reliable in the past, as the original Visual Dictionary called Season 2 "Rise of the Green Ninja" for example, but that error is corrected here, indicating they are aware of the more accurate names for the installments.

(Note: this change would also mean not capitalizing "pilot" and "mini" unless it was at the beginning of a section or sentence.) This would go with the recent vote about not capitalizing titles if they are only descriptive names, but I wanted to make a vote for this on its own since these are very notable pages to change.

As for Season 4, the change would be removing "The". So far I don't know what the original source was for the "The", but the Visual Dictionary New Edition omits the "The", as does the Dark Island Trilogy, Part 2 Episode Guide, so I think it is the correct title. I heard the past Cartoon Network website refers to it with "The", but I don't think that is as much of a reliable a source as two of the official books together, because Cartoon Network is only the distributor, not official Ninjago media on its own.

The mascot characters are not always representative of who is the main character in the series, but they are listed in the intro description even if they are not in the show, because they are closely tied to the branding of the season. Specifically, S8 and 9 had different intro characters than the ones who were on the boxes, but the box characters are still listed in the intro. This is because most often, the box characters can also be considered the focus characters of the seasons. I think this is the same with the collectible items, where they are not always the most important items in the season, but they usually are (S2, 5, and possibly 4 are the seasons where the main items in the show do not correspond to the ones in the sets). So it is better to include them in spite of a few unimportant ones rather than not including any of them due to these few unimportant ones. Wikifan988 (talk) 02:12, 1 January 2021 (UTC)

I don't quite understand why people are opposing. I mean, yeah, I understand that this wiki is only about the show, but Wikifan and Legoninjagofan's points are very strong, so I don't see much of a reason of opposing. Imo, I think this is the right move to make, so we can spread more information, plus the Ninja have either used or collected the collectible items in each season, so I believe it is an important factor to include in the intro description. I don't see why this should be exclusive to the sets.

Toa brings up an interesting idea, so I wonder if there could be a paragraph in the Sets sections of each season page where we talk about the significant traits of the sets and how closely they relate to the season. We could move the mention of a mascot character here, and this is where we could mention the collectible items. It could talk about which aspects of the show the sets focus on, and if there are significant settings in the season that are not featured in the sets or significant differences between the sets and the season, such as how there are no Ivory City/Kingdom of Shintaro sets in the S13 wave and how the Geckles and Munce are portrayed as villains in the sets. This could also talk about the box art and the branding surrounding the season, such as the note I added to the S4 page trivia recently about how the Tournament of Elements sets look to take place in a jungle setting even though the jungle is only the location of a few episodes. We could also mention which waves marked the beginnings and ends of various trends such as spinners, Airjitzu Flyers, etc. While these types of notes could all be in trivia as well, I think it could be helpful to have a section dedicated to it, in order to group similar information together and to have the trivia sections be more concise for other show-related information. Also, it could be more helpful for newcomers who are not as familiar with the set/show relationship and may not understand things that others have come to expect.
